🌏 Weekly Intelligence Report

EDGE Critical Minerals GeoIntel
Week 25  ·  2026

📅 15 June 2026 📊 REE · K-Th-U Prospecting 🌎 Web Researched 🇪🇺 Ireland · EU · Scandinavia · UK · Global

1. Funding, Grants, and Investment Opportunities

Top Picks for EDGE

1. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — RIS Innovation (Deadline 24 June 2026 — 9 days away)
The most time-critical funding window. Ireland qualifies under the RIS (Regional Innovation Scheme) for up to €1M per project (two-phase: €500K validation + €500K scale-up). Covers exploration, sustainable mining, processing, and circular economy. RIS Innovation requires at least 2 organisations from different RIS-eligible countries representing at least two sides of the knowledge triangle. Co-funding up to 70%.

  • Funding Body: EIT RawMaterials
  • Stage: RIS Innovation (TRL 3→8)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €1M total per project
  • Why EDGE fits: Directly covers exploration innovation; Irish entities eligible for RIS-enhanced terms; AI/ML prospecting platform aligns with scope
  • Eligibility: Min 2 organisations from different RIS countries; knowledge triangle representation
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 and 16 October 2026
  • URL: EIT RawMaterials — RIS Innovation Call ↗

2. EIC STEP Scale-Up Pilot — €300M for Deep-Tech Growth (Deadline 25 Nov 2026)
A new pilot under the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP) Regulation, specifically for larger scale-up companies. Provides €10M–€30M in equity-only financing (no grant component). Targets deep-tech companies in digital, cleantech, and biotech, including critical raw materials. Candidates must be raising a €50M–€150M funding round. EDGE should monitor this as a potential Series A/B pathway if growth-stage readiness is reached.

  • Funding Body: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Stage: Scale-up (equity-only)
  • Ticket Size: €10M–€30M per company
  • Why EDGE fits: CRM within scope; potential pathway for later-stage capital if EDGE reaches growth milestones
  • Eligibility: SMEs and small mid-caps (up to 499 employees); must have secured initial investment
  • Deadline: 25 November 2026
  • URL: EIC STEP Scale-Up ↗

3. EIC Accelerator — Critical Raw Materials Challenge (€50M, Next Step 2 Cut-off 8 Jul 2026)
Blended finance for deep-tech SMEs. Up to €2.5M grant plus up to €10M+ equity for TRL 6→8/9 technologies. The CRM challenge has a dedicated €50M budget with thematic evaluation panels. Step 1 short proposals are evaluated on a continuous monthly basis. Step 2 full proposals due 8 July, 2 September, and 4 November 2026.

  • Funding Body: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Stage: Accelerator (TRL 6→8/9)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity
  • Why EDGE fits: Direct CRM challenge includes exploration technologies; single-SME accessible
  • Eligibility: Single innovative SME; deep-tech innovation and growth potential
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026; Step 1 continuous monthly
  • URL: Zabala — EIC Accelerator 2026 ↗

Additional Opportunities

  • EBRD-EU Joint Facility for Critical Raw Materials Exploration (Up to €100M): Equity investments for early-stage junior mining companies exploring CRMs including REE. EU Member States (including Ireland as EU member) and Horizon Europe associated countries eligible. Targets 5–10 junior SMEs with equity instruments. Ongoing — no fixed deadline. URL: EuroAccess — Exploration Call ↗
  • Innovate UK CLIMATES Programme — Circular Critical Materials Supply Chains: Second round expected later in 2026. The first round awarded £6.6M to 16 projects including rare earth magnet recycling. Strand 2 focuses on feasibility studies and R&D for UK critical mineral supply chains. URL: Innovate UK — CLIMATES ↗
  • Horizon Europe — Advanced Recovery of CRMs from WEEE (Deadline 17 Sep 2026, €10M): Recycling and recovery of critical raw materials from electronic waste, including rare earth elements. RIA with €5M per project. Consortium-based. Relevant for REE value chain positioning. URL: Cyprus Funding Portal — WEEE Call ↗
  • SPRIND Tech Metal Transformation Challenge (Germany, Up to €6M): Disruptive technologies for critical/precious metals recovery at industrial scale. DEScycle recently selected with an initial €1.5M award. Rolling applications. URL: DEScycle — SPRIND Award ↗
  • EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — Upscaling (TRL 5→8, €500K–€2.5M+): For validated technologies needing demonstration and market entry. Minimum 50% co-funding. Covers exploration and mining, advanced materials, circular economy. Two cut-offs: 24 June and 16 October 2026. URL: Innovation Place — KAVA 14 Upscaling ↗

2. Scale-Up, Accelerator and Commercialisation Programmes

1. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — RIS Innovation
Co-funding for early-to-mid-stage innovation in EIT RIS countries including Ireland. Targets exploration, sustainable mining, processing, reuse, and materials substitution at TRL 3→8. Two-phase structure with a total maximum of €1M per project.

  • Organiser: EIT RawMaterials
  • Focus: CRM innovation in RIS countries including exploration technologies
  • Funding: Up to €1M per project (two-phase)
  • Cohort timing: Two cut-offs: 24 June 2026 and 16 October 2026
  • What they offer: Co-funding up to 70%, business acceleration, EIT community access, industrial partner networking
  • URL: EIT RawMaterials — RIS Call ↗

2. EIC Accelerator — Blended Finance for Deep-Tech Scale-Up
Both grant funding (up to €2.5M) and equity investment (up to €10M+) for deep-tech SMEs. The 2026 Work Programme includes five strategic challenges, with "Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials Value Chain" (€50M) being the most directly relevant.

  • Organiser: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Focus: Disruptive deep-tech innovation in CRM value chain (TRL 6→8/9)
  • Funding: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity
  • Cohort timing: Rolling Step 1; Step 2 cut-offs 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026
  • What they offer: Blended finance, EIC Business Acceleration Services, coaching, investor access
  • URL: RASPH — EIC Accelerator Updates ↗

3. EIC STEP Scale-Up Pilot (€300M, Opens 2026)
New equity-only pilot for scale-ups with game-changing innovations in digital, cleantech, and biotech, including CRM. €10M–€30M per company. Successful applicants receive a Sovereignty (STEP) Seal. Requires matching private investment at €50M–€150M round level.

  • Organiser: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Focus: Deep-tech scale-up; CRM included in scope
  • Funding: €10M–€30M equity-only
  • Cohort timing: Deadline 25 November 2026
  • What they offer: Equity investment, STEP Seal, access to EU programmes and investors
  • URL: Segler Consulting — EIC 2026 Topics ↗

4. ESA BIC — Business Incubation for Space Downstream Applications
ESA BICs across Europe support startups using space technology for Earth-based applications including mineral exploration via satellite data and remote sensing. Regional centres offer rolling applications with up to €50K–€200K funding, technical support, and business mentoring. An ESA BIC Noordwijk participant (Terraprisma) highlighted for mineral exploration using satellite intelligence.

  • Organiser: European Space Agency (ESA) via national ESA BIC hosts
  • Focus: Space technology downstream for Earth observation, remote sensing, mineral exploration
  • What they offer: Up to €50K–€200K funding, incubation, technical mentoring, ESA network
  • Cohort timing: Rolling applications per regional BIC
  • URL: ESA BIC Noordwijk 2026 Info Session ↗

5. ESA BSGN Space Resources Industry Accelerator
The Business in Space Growth Network accelerator focuses on advancing technologies for the lunar space resources value chain, including regolith processing and resource extraction relevant to planetary prospecting. A new call for projects expected Q4 2026 – Q1 2027. Operated by ESA and ESRIC Luxembourg.

  • Organiser: ESA / ESRIC Luxembourg
  • Focus: Space resources value chain technologies
  • What they offer: Acceleration, technical mentorship, ESA network
  • Cohort timing: Next call expected Q4 2026 – Q1 2027
  • URL: ESA BSGN — Space Resources Accelerator ↗

3. Training, Workshops and Courses

1. World Mining Congress 2026 — Short Courses (22–23 June 2026, Lima, Peru)
Sixteen high-level short courses running alongside the WMC. Topics include AI applied to mining operations, critical minerals, decarbonisation, and next-generation exploration. Four- and eight-hour intensive sessions in English. Official certificate from the Peruvian Institute of Mining Engineers. Registration via the WMC portal.

  • Organiser: Peruvian Institute of Mining Engineers / WMC 2026
  • Location: Lima, Peru (IIMP headquarters)
  • Dates: 22–23 June 2026 (pre-congress)
  • Level: Professional
  • Cost: Registration via WMC portal
  • URL: WMC 2026 — Short Courses ↗

2. "AI-Powered Mineral Resource Development" International Summer School (13–26 July 2026, Zhuhai, China)
Two-week summer school at Sun Yat-sen University covering geoscience big data, intelligent prospecting, and AI for mineral exploration. Includes academic lectures, field trips, and group discussions. No registration fee; accommodation and meals covered by the organisers. Participants cover their own airfare.

  • Organiser: Sun Yat-sen University, China
  • Location: Zhuhai, China (in-person)
  • Dates: 13–26 July 2026
  • Level: Graduate / Senior undergraduate
  • Cost: Free (registration fee waived; accommodation and meals provided)
  • Scholarship options: Local costs covered; airfare not included
  • URL: SYSU — AI-Powered Mineral Resource Summer School ↗

3. SEG — Probabilistic Deep Learning Inversion for Critical Mineral Exploration
Two-day online short course covering GANs, conditional VAEs, invertible neural networks, and normalizing flows for geophysical inverse problems in mineral exploration. Taught by Prof. Jiajia Sun (University of Houston). Includes hands-on coding exercises. Prerequisites include working knowledge of deep learning and undergraduate geophysics. Available on-demand.

  • Organiser: Society of Exploration Geophysicists (SEG)
  • Location: Online (on-demand)
  • Level: Advanced Professional
  • URL: SEG — Deep Learning Course ↗

4. IRTC — Raw Materials Risk Manager (ISO/IEC 17024 Certified) — 29 Jun–2 Jul 2026
Four-morning online course covering critical raw material risk identification, EU criticality assessment methodology, mitigation options, and regulatory frameworks. Certified in accordance with ISO/IEC 17024. Directly relevant for CRM risk assessment capability within EDGE.

  • Organiser: International Raw Materials Training Centre (IRTC)
  • Location: Online
  • Dates: 29 June – 2 July 2026 (09:30–12:15 CET daily)
  • Level: Professional/CPD
  • Cost: €700 regular / €560 students & EuroGeol holders (exam extra: €250)
  • URL: IRTC Online Training ↗

5. 18th MiningForum Berlin — Conference & Training (18–19 June 2026, Berlin)
"Raw Materials Momentum" theme with 400+ experts, 40+ sessions in 4 parallel tracks covering CRM supply, CRMA implementation, mining tech and digitalisation. Partnered with RWTH Aachen University. Strong policy and industry focus with dedicated sessions on rare earths and lithium.

  • Organiser: MiningForum / partner organisations
  • Location: Estrel Hotel, Berlin, Germany
  • Dates: 18–19 June 2026
  • Level: Professional / Executive
  • Cost: Standard conference fees apply
  • URL: MiningForum Berlin 2026 Agenda ↗

4. Conferences, Events and Partnering Opportunities

Must-Attend for EDGE

1. MiningForum Berlin — 18–19 June 2026, Berlin, Germany
A premier European critical raw materials gathering with 400+ delegates from policy, industry, and research. Four parallel tracks cover CRMA implementation, rare earth supply security, lithium and battery metals, and mining technology/digitalisation. Partnered with RWTH Aachen University. The timing (this week) makes it immediately actionable.

  • Organiser: MiningForum / RWTH Aachen University
  • Audience: 400+ policy-makers, industry executives, researchers, investors
  • Why attend: Immediate opportunity (this week); rare earth supply security is a core theme; strong EU policy focus with CRMA implementation sessions
  • URL: MiningForum Berlin 2026 ↗

2. Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference — 15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest
Europe's leading battery raw materials gathering. Senior leaders across the full battery supply chain — miners, processors, cathode/cell manufacturers, OEMs, recyclers, traders, and policymakers. Topics include LFP adoption, lithium and critical mineral demand, EU battery regulations, battery passports, and black mass recycling.

  • Organiser: Fastmarkets
  • Audience: 300+ professionals across the battery raw materials value chain
  • Why attend: Direct access to offtake partners and investors; REE demand outlook for permanent magnets in EVs; essential for understanding downstream demand signals
  • URL: Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials ↗

3. Resourcing Tomorrow / Mines and Money London — 1–3 Dec 2026, London
Europe's largest mining investment event, featuring the Critical Minerals Ministerial Roundtable. Attracts 1,000+ mining executives, investors, and government officials. EDGE should prioritise this for investor networking, partnership development, and understanding the institutional investment landscape for CRM exploration technologies.

  • Organiser: Mines and Money
  • Audience: 1,000+ mining executives, investors, government officials
  • Why attend: Premier mining investment event in Europe; Critical Minerals Ministerial provides direct policy access; strong UK government participation
  • URL: Resourcing Tomorrow ↗

4. Mining & Critical Minerals Europe Conference & Exhibition — 20–21 Oct 2026, London
Co-located with LME Week and the MMTA Critical Materials Forum. Covers mining, critical minerals supply chains, technology, and investment. Over 200 senior executives expected from 30+ countries. Strong UK government participation. EDGE could present its AI/ML platform to an audience of international mining companies and investors.

  • Organiser: Spire Events
  • Audience: Mining executives, critical minerals specialists, investors, government
  • Why attend: London location maximises accessibility; co-located with LME Week; strong government and industry crossover
  • URL: Mining & Critical Minerals Europe ↗

5. IAGOD 16th Quadrennial Symposium — 30 Aug–2 Sep 2026, Porto, Portugal
"The Role of Geoscience in the Energy Transition" theme with dedicated critical minerals sessions. Academic and industry audience focused on mineral deposit geology, geochemistry, and exploration. Opportunity for EDGE to present scientific results and build R&D partnerships with European research groups.

  • Organiser: IAGOD / Universidade do Porto
  • Audience: Economic geologists, researchers, exploration professionals
  • Why attend: Strong academic focus allows EDGE to present AI/ML prospecting methodology; R&D consortium building opportunity
  • URL: IAGOD 2026 ↗

Additional Events

  • ECOMONDO 2026 — Earth Observation for Sustainable CRM Management — 3–6 Nov 2026, Rimini, Italy. Session on Copernicus and satellite data for CRM exploration and monitoring. URL: ECOMONDO ↗
  • Exploring Together — Responsible Critical Raw Materials Event — 17 June 2026, University of Oviedo, Spain. Responsible exploitation of critical raw materials in Europe. URL: ISMC — Exploring Together ↗
  • SEG Critical Commodities Workshop — 10–12 Nov 2026, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Integrated geoscience signatures for critical commodities (Cu, REE, Li, Au). URL: SEG Workshop ↗
  • SITE Energy Talk 2026 — 15 April 2026 (past), Stockholm School of Economics. Recordings may be available for the "Critical minerals and the new geopolitics of the green transition" session. URL: SITE Energy Talk ↗

5. Research, R&D and Collaboration Calls

Top 5 Fits for EDGE

1. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — RIS Innovation (Up to €1M, deadline 24 Jun 2026)
The most urgent R&D funding window. Supports TRL 3→8 innovation in RIS countries including Ireland. EDGE should urgently assess whether a consortium with an Irish research partner (TCD, UCD, UL) and a European geological survey can be assembled for the June cut-off, or target the 16 October 2026 fallback.

  • Programme: EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14
  • TRL: 3→8 (RIS Innovation)
  • Lead type: Consortium (min 2 organisations from different RIS countries)
  • Budget: Up to €1M total
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 and 16 October 2026
  • URL: EIT RawMaterials — RIS Call ↗

2. HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 — Reducing Dependence on CRMs Through Advanced Materials (€36M)
Flagship 2027 Innovation Action targeting TRL 5–7 demonstration projects for breakthrough materials and processes reducing CRM dependency. The value chain scope from exploration through processing creates an entry point for EDGE's prospecting intelligence platform. Opens 22 September 2026, deadline 2 February 2027.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4
  • TRL: 5–7 (IA)
  • Lead type: Consortium (3+ partners from different MS/AC)
  • Budget: €36M total (~€5–8M per project)
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: Microfluidics Innovation — MAT-PROD-22 ↗

3. HORIZON-CL4-2026-01-MAT-PROD-11 — Innovative Technologies for Exploration & Data Modelling of Raw Materials (€18.5M)
A direct fit for EDGE's AI/ML platform. This RIA explicitly requires AI/ML methods for geological modelling, mineral prospectivity prediction, and multi-source data integration. Supports CRMA Article 19 (National Exploration Programmes). Deadline 21 April 2026 has passed, but proposals may still be under evaluation — monitor for future calls under the Raw Materials Partnership.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4
  • TRL: 3–5 (RIA)
  • Lead type: Consortium
  • Budget: €18.5M total (€5–7M per project)
  • Deadline: 21 April 2026 (passed; monitor for next cycle)
  • URL: Africa Europe Innovation — Exploration Call ↗

4. EIC Accelerator — Critical Raw Materials Challenge (€50M)
Directly accessible single-SME R&D funding with blended finance (grant + equity). The CRM challenge supports TRL 6→8/9 technologies. EDGE should target the 8 July or 2 September 2026 cut-off given the EIT RawMaterials KAVA 14 timeline. The Step 1 short proposal is evaluated on a continuous monthly basis.

  • Programme: EIC Accelerator (Challenge-based)
  • TRL: 6→8/9
  • Lead type: Single SME (can include partners)
  • Budget: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity; €50M overall for the CRM challenge
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026; Step 1 continuous monthly
  • URL: GrantBite — EIC Accelerator Overview ↗

5. Proposed European Partnership on Raw Materials for the Green & Digital Transition (Starting 2026)
A co-funded European Partnership coordinating Member States' R&I funding on critical raw materials across the full value chain (exploration, extraction, processing, recycling). Joint calls co-funded by the EU designed to support CRMA implementation. EDGE should monitor for the first call topics and deadlines.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe / European Commission
  • TRL: Basic research to demonstration (full range)
  • Lead type: Consortium (Member State coordination)
  • Budget: TBC (co-funded partnership)
  • Deadline: First calls expected late 2026 / early 2027
  • URL: EC Candidate List — European Partnerships ↗

6. Policy, Regulation and Strategic Context

European Union — CRMA Implementation Accelerates

EU Council Position on CRMA Amendments (March 2026): The EU Council adopted its negotiating position on 4 March 2026, proposing centralised Commission oversight of large companies' CRM supply chains. Key provisions include risk-mitigation measures for single-supplier dependence, Digital Product Passports for permanent magnets, and recycled content alignment with eco-design rules. Negotiations with the European Parliament are pending, with adoption of amendments expected by mid-2027.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: IEU Monitoring — EU Council Position ↗

RESourceEU Action Plan — First Deliverables Underway: The European Critical Raw Materials Centre is being established in 2026, modelled on Japan's JOGMEC, to steer investment, coordinate joint purchasing, and manage strategic stockpiles. The Raw Materials Mechanism matchmaking tool launched November 2025, with the first matchmaking round held in March 2026. Export restrictions on permanent magnet scrap and aluminium scrap are being implemented in Q2 2026. Lithium-ion battery waste exports to non-OECD countries will be banned from September 2026.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Chambers and Partners — RESourceEU Analysis ↗

Second CRMA Strategic Projects Round — Results Pending: Over 160 applications were received for the second round (cut-off 15 January 2026), including 95 from within the EU and 66 from outside. Of these, 75 projects support the battery value chain and 21 focus on rare earth elements for permanent magnets. The European Commission is still assessing applications and consulting with Member States. Results are expected in mid-2026. Strategic status unlocks accelerated permitting (27 months extraction, 15 months processing), RESourceEU financing access, and offtake certainty.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: 2EU Brussels — Second Strategic Projects Round ↗

CRM Board Strategic Stockpiling — First Reporting Deadline 24 May 2026: Member States have submitted their first reports on strategic stocks of critical and strategic raw materials. The European Commission is developing a draft benchmark for safe stockpiling levels. A pilot stockpiling project was launched by several Member States and the Commission in early 2026, with rare earths, tungsten, and gallium shortlisted. EU countries can count stockpiling contributions toward NATO's 1.5% GDP defence spending commitment.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union / NATO
  • URL: Gleiss Lutz — RESourceEU Investor Impact ↗

Scandinavia — European Rare Earth Hub Emerges

Norway Fen Deposit — Government Takes Over Permitting: Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced the Norwegian state will assume responsibility for zoning and permitting of the Fen rare earth deposit in Telemark. The deposit holds 15.9 million tonnes of rare earth oxides, making it Europe's largest known REE deposit (~19% NdPr). First production targeted for late 2031. A Letter of Intent with Copenhagen Atomics will supply thorium for next-generation molten salt nuclear reactors. Environmental opposition remains a key challenge.

  • Jurisdiction: Norway
  • URL: Energy News — Fen Deposit ↗

Norra Kärr Mining Lease — Swedish Government Decision Pending: The Swedish Mining Inspectorate has recommended approval of the mining lease for Leading Edge Materials' Norra Kärr HREE project, with every government agency in the permitting process recommending approval. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium) with an initial 26-year mine life. An MoU with Ascension Earth Resources will test proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples.

  • Jurisdiction: Sweden
  • URL: Globe and Mail — Norra Kärr ↗

United Kingdom — Critical Minerals Diplomacy

UK–US Critical Minerals MoU (February 2026): The UK and US signed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals covering coordinated investment, joint project selection, streamlined permitting, and cooperation on pricing, recycling, geological mapping, and national security reviews. A Mining, Minerals and Metals Investment Ministerial is to convene within 180 days. The UK now has bilateral agreements with the US, Australia, and Canada.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom / United States
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Critical Minerals MoU ↗

Northern Ireland — Review of Mineral Licensing: A call for evidence on mineral licensing reform was published in Northern Ireland, aligning with UK Critical Minerals Strategy and EU CRMA objectives. This is relevant for EDGE's Irish operations as it may affect cross-border exploration regulation and licensing frameworks.

  • Jurisdiction: Northern Ireland / UK
  • URL: Economy NI — Mineral Licensing Review ↗

Ireland — National Exploration Programme Delayed

Ireland's CRMA National Exploration Programme Behind Schedule: Under Article 19 of the CRMA, Ireland was required to establish a national exploration programme by May 2025. A technical report due by end of 2024 has been delayed due to a "continued lack of staff resources" at Geological Survey Ireland (Department of Climate). Work is not expected to begin until an entry-level geologist is appointed in early 2026, with a senior geologist competition later in the year. Reporting is expected to be completed during 2027. The Department may consider procuring external services if needed. This delay represents both a gap and an opportunity for EDGE to position its AI/ML prospecting platform as a capacity multiplier for under-resourced geological surveys.

  • Jurisdiction: Ireland
  • URL: PA Media — Ireland Exploration Programme Delayed ↗

Geopolitical Context — China's Rare Earth Dominance Intensifies

Yttrium Prices Surge ~140–150x Since April 2025 Controls: China's export licensing on heavy rare earths (April 2025) has caused an extraordinary price surge. Yttrium metal prices rose approximately 69–150 times in ex-China markets. Exports of yttrium, dysprosium, and terbium are running at just 42%, 41%, and 49% respectively of pre-restriction volumes. The October 2025 extraterritorial controls were suspended for one year (expires November 2026), but the April 2025 controls remain fully in force. Some US aerospace companies have temporarily paused production due to yttrium shortages.

  • Jurisdiction: Global / China
  • URL: Yahoo Finance — China's Rare Earth Grip Holds ↗

China's New Mineral Resources Law Regulations (June 2026): China enacted new Mineral Resources Law regulations introducing national security reviews for foreign mining investments and fast-tracking strategic mineral reserve buildout. This signals even tighter full-chain oversight extending beyond rare earths to other critical minerals. The US Pentagon has taken a $400M equity stake in MP Materials, and $1.6B has been committed to USA Rare Earth for a Texas deposit and processing facility. The US NDAA will prohibit federal purchase of Chinese-processed rare earth materials from 2027 onward.

  • Jurisdiction: Global
  • URL: Canadian Mining Journal — China Mining Controls ↗

Implementation Challenges Persist in EU CRM Strategy: A joint policy brief from 11 Horizon Europe projects highlights that Europe's main risk is not resource scarcity but delayed implementation. Key bottlenecks include financing gaps for first-of-a-kind plants, fragmented regulatory practices, permitting complexity, and social acceptance challenges. The European Court of Auditors (February 2026) found that EU diversification efforts have produced "no tangible results" so far, with domestic processing capacity declining.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: RemHub — CRMA Implementation Challenge ↗

7. Action List for This Week

[HIGH] Urgent: Evaluate EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 RIS Innovation window (deadline 24 Jun 2026 — 9 days): With only 9 days remaining, assess whether a consortium with an Irish research partner can be assembled for the RIS Innovation stream (up to €1M). Ireland qualifies for enhanced RIS terms. If the June cut-off is not feasible, prepare a strong application for the 16 October 2026 second cut-off. The EIT RawMaterials partner network (50+ core partners, 200+ associated) provides a ready-made consortium-building pool.

[HIGH] Submit EIC Accelerator Step 1 short proposal for the CRM Challenge (targeting 8 Jul 2026 Step 2 cut-off): The 12-page short proposal, 10-slide pitch deck, and 3-minute video can be prepared in 3–4 weeks. Step 1 is evaluated on a continuous monthly basis. Target the 8 July Step 2 cut-off as the primary deadline, with 2 September as the fallback. The CRM challenge has a dedicated €50M budget with thematic evaluation panels — the most directly accessible single-SME funding pathway for EDGE's AI/ML platform.

[HIGH] Monitor MiningForum Berlin (18–19 Jun 2026) outcomes remotely: Even if EDGE cannot attend in person at short notice, monitor the outcomes of the MiningForum Berlin sessions on rare earth supply security and CRMA implementation. Key outcomes may inform EDGE's policy positioning and identify potential consortium partners for upcoming R&D calls.

[MEDIUM] Register for Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference (15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest) before rate increase: Standard rate is €2,145 (plus 27% Hungarian VAT). Register before the early-bird expiry. This conference provides direct access to battery OEMs and offtakers who are end-users of REEs and lithium in permanent magnets — a prime opportunity for commercial pilot partner identification and downstream demand intelligence.

[MEDIUM] Prepare Horizon Europe consortium strategy for MAT-PROD-22 (opens 22 Sep 2026, €36M budget): With a February 2027 deadline, begin identifying potential consortium partners from the EIT RawMaterials network, Irish research groups (TCD, UCD, UL, NUIG), and European geological surveys. The 3–4 month preparation window allows for a competitive proposal linking AI prospecting with downstream CRM processing. Target TRL 5–7 demonstration.

[MEDIUM] Track second CRMA Strategic Projects round results: The European Commission is expected to announce selected projects from the second round (160+ applications, including 21 REE-focused) in mid-2026. Monitor for the outcome list — it will signal priority investment areas and identify consortia EDGE could partner with. Particular attention to rare earth and exploration technology projects.

[MEDIUM] Assess engagement strategy for Ireland's delayed National Exploration Programme: With Geological Survey Ireland significantly behind on the CRMA-mandated exploration programme (report expected 2027), EDGE should prepare a capability brief positioning its AI/ML platform as a force multiplier for under-resourced geological surveys. This could open a domestic service contract pathway leveraging Ireland's RIS eligibility.

[MEDIUM] Monitor yttrium and HREE price trends for exploration targeting signals: Yttrium prices have surged ~140–150x since April 2025 Chinese export controls. Sustained high prices for heavy rare earths strengthen the economic case for non-Chinese HREE exploration. The one-year suspension of October 2025 controls expires November 2026, creating a potential further price catalyst. Use these market signals to prioritise exploration targets with HREE potential.

[MEDIUM] Track Norway Fen deposit and Norra Kärr permitting decisions: The Norwegian state's takeover of Fen deposit planning represents significant de-risking of Europe's largest REE deposit. A positive Swedish government decision on Norra Kärr would further validate Europe's HREE potential. Both developments strengthen the policy narrative supporting CRM exploration technology investment in Europe.

[LOW] Explore ESA BIC application for space-tech downstream mineral exploration: The ESA Business Incubation Centre model offers up to €200K in funding and technical mentoring for companies applying satellite data and remote sensing to mineral exploration. The Terraprisma success story demonstrates proof of concept. ESA BICs operate with rolling applications across multiple European centres — a low-effort parallel funding track.

  - **Total max: €1 million** per project
- Duration: Up to **2 years** (all activities must be completed by **December 2028**)

### 🎯 Focus Areas
- Exploration & sustainable mining
- Raw materials processing & refining
- Advanced materials
- Circular economy & recycling

---

## 📰 Top News: Companies Selected for 2026 EIC Accelerator

### 🇸🇪 Altris (Sweden) – Sodium-ion Battery Materials
- Selected for the **2026 EIC Accelerator** cohort to scale its patented **sodium-ion battery electrodes**, which replace expensive lithium and cobalt with abundant, low-cost sodium.
- The funding will accelerate production capacity, expand technological footprint, and support partnerships with European battery manufacturers.
- Source: [Gulf Oil & Gas News](https://gulfoilandgas.com/webpro1/main/mainnews.asp?id=1109258) (March 2026)

### 🇫🇷 Mecaware (France) – Critical Metals Recycling
- Selected for the **2026 EIC Accelerator** to industrialize the recycling of critical battery metals (**lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper**) in Europe.
- Awarded **€2.5M grant + up to €10M equity**.
- Its closed-loop hydrometallurgical process produces battery-grade metal salts with no sulfate effluents and limited energy consumption.
- A pilot plant in **Béthune, France**, is scheduled to begin operations by **end of 2026**, targeting **8,000 tons of strategic metals per year by 2029**.
- Source: [Mecaware official announcement](https://www.mecaware.com/en/actualite/mecaware-laureat-de-leic-accelerator-pour-industrialiser-le-recyclage-des-metaux-critiques-des-batteries-en-europe) (Feb 2026)

### 🇫🇮 Sensmet (Finland) – Water Monitoring for Critical Raw Materials
- Awarded **€2.5M EIC Accelerator grant** + **€1.5M from EIT RawMaterials**.
- Its µDOES® technology enables **continuous, real-time multi-metal analysis** of aqueous samples, supporting more efficient production and recycling of critical raw materials (lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earth elements).
- Aligns with the **EU Critical Raw Materials Act**.
- Source: [Envirotec](https://envirotecmagazine.com/2026/06/04/finnish-firm-wins-e2-5m-award-for-water-monitoring-tech/) (June 2026)

### 🇫🇮 Geyser Batteries (Finland) – Grid-Stabilizing Batteries
- Selected for EIC Accelerator funding for its **water-based battery technology** that **avoids all critical raw materials** (lithium, nickel).
- Focused on grid flexibility and blackout prevention.
- Source: [ArcticStartup](https://arcticstartup.com/page/19/?author=0)

---

## 🗓️ EIC Accelerator 2026 Program Changes

### Increased Budget & More Cut-off Dates
| Item | 2025 | 2026 |
|------|------|------|
| **Total Budget** | €384M | **€414M (Open) + €220M (Challenges) = €634M** |
| **Cut-off Dates** | 2 per year | **6 per year** (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov) |
| **Minimum Blended Finance** | €500K | **€1M** |
| **Max Grant** | €2.5M | €2.5M |
| **Max Equity via EIC Fund** | Up to €15M | Up to **€10M** |

Source: [Zabala](https://www.zabala.eu/news/eic-accelerator-2026-updates/), [Euro-Funding](https://euro-funding.com/en/eic-accelerator/)

### 🎯 New Thematic Challenge: Critical Raw Materials
The **"Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials value chain"** challenge has been allocated **€50 million** (approx. 7% of the total budget). Other challenges include:
- Advanced materials for renewable energy & energy storage (€50M)
- Fusion technologies (€20M)
- Biotech for agricultural soil regeneration (€50M)
- Deep tech for climate adaptation (€50M)

---

## 🔑 Key Takeaways
1. **Critical raw materials are a major strategic priority** for the EIC in 2026, with a dedicated €50M challenge.
2. **Battery recycling and alternative materials** (sodium-ion, water-based batteries) are the dominant themes among selected companies.
3. The **EIC Accelerator has become more competitive and rigorous**, with earlier technical due diligence and a ~4% success rate.
4. All selected companies align with the **EU Critical Raw Materials Act** and the goal of reducing Europe's >96% import dependency for strategic metals.

- Deep tech for climate adaptation (€50M)

Here is a summary of the latest developments based on the search results:

### 1. RESourceEU Action Plan and CRMA Amendments
The **RESourceEU Action Plan**, adopted in December 2025, is now being operationalised. It shifts the EU from policy signals to **direct market intervention** in critical raw materials. Key elements include:

- **European Critical Raw Materials Centre** — to be proposed in 2026, coordinating investment, joint purchasing, and stockpiling
- **€3 billion mobilised** in EU funds (EIB, Battery Booster, Horizon Europe) to fast-track projects

- The **Council** adopted its general approach in **March 2026**
- The **European Parliament** is still preparing its position — expected to push for **stronger circularity**, **binding recycled-content targets**, and **firmer waste definitions**

以下是关于2026年6月中国稀土出口管制对钇价格及供应链中断影响的关键信息：

---

### 1. 出口管制背景

- **2025年4月**，中国对7种重稀土实施出口管制：**钐、钆、铽、镝、镥、钪、钇**（回应美国特朗普政府关税措施）。
- **2026年1月-2月**，中国进一步加强对日本的出口管制，针对日本首相高市早苗涉台言论。
- **2026年6月15日**，《矿产资源法实施条例》正式施行，将36种矿产（含稀土、钨、锂等）列入战略性矿产资源目录。

### 2. 钇（Yttrium）价格暴涨

| 来源 | 价格 | 时间 |
|------|------|------|
| 国内氧化钇报价 | 约 **5.5万元/吨**（人民币） | 2026年6月 |
| 鹿特丹港口价 | **457.50美元/kg**（约45.75万美元/吨） | 2026年6月 |
| 欧洲市场价（百川） | **1,175美元/kg**（约117.5万美元/吨） | 2026年6月 |
| 海外价格涨幅 | 自2025年4月管制以来**上涨约140倍**（Argus数据） | 截至2026年5月 |

**内外价差高达上百倍**，国内5.5万元/吨 vs 海外最高117.5万美元/吨。

### 3. 其他稀土内外价差

- 氧化镝：内外价差约 **8倍**
- 氧化铽：内外价差约 **5倍**
- 氧化钆：内外价差约 **40倍**
- 氧化钪：内外价差约 **6倍**
- 海外价格：镝约 **1,450美元/kg**，铽约 **4,500美元/kg**（2026年5月）

### 4. 供应链中断实际影响

- **日本东曹**已暂停氧化锆粉体供应，国内齿科氧化锆企业收到通知，标志原料短缺从预期走向落地。
- 中国重稀土出口量仍较管制前**下降约50%**。
- 日本自2025年11月以来未收到任何铽、镝氧化物出口，钇氧化物仅微量。
- 稀土磁材出口2026年5月环比下降35%。

### 5. 分析师观点（中信建投，2026年6月22日）

- 海外稀土供给受限导致下游减停产，**国内产业链（上中下游）均将受益**。
- 供应持续偏紧：原矿生产受指标管控，全年指标增幅不超过10%；废料原料受限，部分分离厂停减产。
- 需求端有增加预期：下游企业将开启集中备库，全球地缘冲突常态化拉动军工、战略储备等刚性需求。

### 关键结论

截至**2026年6月**，中国稀土出口管制已造成严重的海外供应中断，**钇价格在海外飙升逾百倍**，稀土内外价差悬殊。日本、欧洲等海外下游制造商面临原料短缺和成本暴涨，而国内稀土产业链有望受益于全球市场份额扩大。

## Norway Fen Rare Earth Deposit: 2026 Permitting & Thorium Update

Here's a summary of the latest developments based on the search results:

### 📈 Resource Upgrade (March–April 2026)

- **Resource estimate increased by 81%** — from 8.8 million tonnes (2024) to **15.9 million tonnes** of total rare earth oxides (TREO), making it the **largest known rare earth deposit in Europe**.
- The updated JORC inferred resource is now reported as **1,083 Mt at 1.31 wt% TREO**, including 0.24 wt% NdPr oxide.
- This dwarfs Sweden's Per Geijer deposit (2.2 Mt TREO) — the previous European record holder.

### 🏛️ Permitting & Government Intervention

- **April 2026**: Norway's government (PM Jonas Gahr Støre) announced it will **take over the planning** of the Fen deposit, citing:
  - **National supply security** — to reduce European reliance on China (95% of EU rare earth imports came from China, Malaysia, and Russia in 2024).
  - **Land-use disputes** — local opposition (including environmental and agricultural groups) posed risks similar to those delaying wind farm developments in Norway.
- The company, **Rare Earths Norway**, holds an **exploitation permit** but still requires an **operating permit**.
- Permitting is reportedly still in process, with some "risk aversion" procedures needed to compete with lower-cost Chinese production.

### 🎯 Production Timeline

| Milestone | Target |
|---|---|
| Start of production | **Late 2030 / 2031** |
| NdPr oxide production | **800 tonnes/year by 2032** |
| EU demand coverage | ~5% of total EU NdPr demand |

### ⚠️ Thorium Content

- The deposit contains **significant thorium (Th)** — a key detail for the Rare Earth industry, as thorium is radioactive and complicates processing.
- The **rødberg** (hematized carbonatite) variety has **high thorium content**, making it "less suitable for industry at the moment."
- The **Fe-dolomite carbonatite** — the main target for exploitation — is the preferred ore type, with lower Th levels.
- The deposit also contains **notable niobium**, which adds economic value alongside the rare earths.

### 🌍 Strategic Importance

- EU passed the **"ResourceEU" Action Plan** (Dec 2025) to accelerate domestic critical mineral mining, refining, and recycling.
- Rare Earths Norway envisions a compact **"ore-to-magnet"** value chain to strengthen European industrial resilience.
- However, the EU has **no restrictions** on where the mined rare earths can be sold, allowing potential exports outside Europe.

---

**Key takeaway:** The Fen deposit has grown significantly in resource size, but the thorium content in certain ore zones remains a processing challenge. The Norwegian government stepped in to accelerate permitting, but the project still needs an operating permit before production (targeted around 2030-2032).

Here is a summary of the key news and developments regarding Ireland's critical minerals exploration in 2026, with a focus on the Geological Survey of Ireland (GSI) and related activity:

## 1. Government Critical Raw Materials Survey Delayed to 2027

A key government survey to identify critical raw materials across Ireland is **years behind schedule** due to a shortage of geologists at the Geological Survey of Ireland. The work — mandated by the EU's Critical Raw Materials Act — was supposed to start in 2024 but is now expected to begin in **early 2026** with the appointment of an entry-level geologist. A senior geologist competition in 2026 would allow completion of the study and reporting during **2027**. Minister for Climate Darragh O'Brien acknowledged the delays and called for "more action, delivered faster."

## 2. PDAC 2026 — Ireland Pavilion Highlights

At the **PDAC 2026** conference (March 1–4 in Toronto), the **Geoscience Policy Division and Geological Survey Ireland** led the Ireland Pavilion. Key figures including **Koen Verbruggen** (GSI) and **Eoin McGrath** (Head of Minerals Programme at GSI) participated in panels on the EU Critical Raw Materials Act and EuroGeoSurveys seminars. They highlighted promising developments including the **Ballywire copper-lead-zinc-silver discovery** by Group Eleven and recent investments by the **Irish Minerals Fund**.

## 3. Group Eleven's Ballywire Discovery — Major 2026 Results

The most significant exploration news in Ireland in 2026 comes from **Group Eleven Resources** at its Ballywire discovery in the Limerick Basin:

- **June 11, 2026:** Drilling returned 23.60% Cu, 506 g/t Ag, and 2.04% Sb over 0.6m (some of the highest copper grades in Ireland in 60 years). Nine Cu-Ag zones were intersected, with four rigs active.
- **May 28, 2026:** An 80m step-out hole returned 62.5m of 5.6% Zn+Pb (including 11.8m of 13.4% Zn+Pb), and a **720m step-out** confirmed deeper Cu-Ag mineralization, suggesting the system may extend across the entire 3.2km discovery.
- The company raised **C$12 million** in March 2026, funding a drill program expansion from 20,000m to **67,000–75,000m** over approximately two years.
- Ballywire is now recognized as Ireland's **most significant mineral discovery in over a decade**, with a 6km prospective trend of which only ~25% has been systematically drilled.

## 4. Lithium Exploration in Southeast Ireland

A 2026 study published in *Mineralium Deposita* (Vol. 61, Issue 5) by Kaeter and Menuge examined **columbite-tantalite and cassiterite as indicator minerals for lithium pegmatites** in the Leinster Batholith region of southeast Ireland. The research demonstrates that stream-sediment geochemistry and mineralogy can effectively identify lithium-cesium-tantalum (LCT) spodumene pegmatites, supporting ongoing exploration for lithium — a critical raw material for the energy transition.

## 5. GSI Lecture on Net Zero & Geoscience (January 2026)

Geological Survey Ireland held a joint lecture with the Royal Irish Academy titled **"Why does net zero need geoscience?"** featuring Karen Hanghøj (Director, British Geological Survey). The talk covered critical raw material supply chains, circular economy considerations, and geopolitical dimensions. Panelists included Eoin McGrath (GSI) and academics from University College Cork and Trinity College Dublin.

## 6. EU Critical Raw Materials Act Context

The EU CRMA is shaping Irish exploration strategy, with targets of **10% domestic extraction** and **40% domestic processing** of strategic raw materials by 2030. Copper, antimony, germanium, and lithium are designated critical, giving projects like Ballywire potential access to streamlined permitting — though no project has yet formally qualified.

---

**In summary:** 2026 is a pivotal year for Irish critical minerals — with significant private-sector exploration success at Ballywire, active government policy development around the EU CRMA, but also notable delays at the Geological Survey of Ireland due to staffing shortages.

The UK government announced a **£50 million ($66 million) critical minerals investment package** on **22 June 2026**, aimed at reducing reliance on imports (particularly from China) and strengthening domestic supply chains.

### Key Details

**Announcement Date:** 22 June 2026
**Announced by:** Industry Minister **Chris McDonald**, during a visit to the **Wilton Centre in Teesside** (northeast England)

### Funding Breakdown — Three Pillars

| Pillar | Amount | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **Magnet Hub** | **£20 million** | Establish a world-class national facility to develop, test, and scale up **rare earth magnet manufacturing**, including skills and training |
| **Critical Minerals Accelerator** | **£25 million** | Support collaborative projects across **extraction, processing, and recycling** of critical minerals to accelerate innovation and commercialisation |
| **Demand Aggregation Platform** | **Up to £5 million** | Help UK industry consolidate and pool critical mineral demand across sectors to unlock investment and secure supply through strategic partnerships |

### Strategic Context

- Builds on **over £200 million** already committed to the UK critical minerals sector
- Aim: Reduce dependence on **China**, which controls ~70% of global rare earth mining and ~90% of refining
- Supports the UK's **Critical Minerals Strategy** and aligns with the government's **Industrial Strategy**
- Part of broader efforts including international partnerships with the **US and South Korea**

### Related Development

The announcement follows the **opening of Britain's first commercial rare earth magnet plant in 25 years** — operated by **Mkango Resources' HyProMag unit in Birmingham** — which uses recycled materials to produce magnets for electric motors and other technologies.

### Source

Official UK Government announcement: [UK to secure critical minerals boosting economic resilience and cutting reliance on imports](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-to-secure-critical-minerals-boosting-economic-resilience-and-cutting-reliance-on-imports) (published 22 June 2026)

### 1. G7 Sets Up Critical Minerals Alliance & Platform to Cut Reliance on China
**Date:** June 17–18, 2026 | **Source:** Reuters, CNBC TV18, US News

At the G7 Summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, leaders agreed to:
- Reduce dependence on any single supplier of **rare earths and permanent magnets** to **below 60% by 2030** (with an ambition of 50%).
- Launch a **G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance**, coordinated with the **IEA and OECD**, for policy coordination, data sharing, stockpiling, and crisis response — including "early warnings of market distortions."
- Pilot traceability and transparency mechanisms starting with **lithium and nickel**, expanding to **five new critical minerals each year** with a focus on rare earths.
- Explore **joint procurement, price-gap subsidies, quotas, and price floors** to support non-Chinese supply chains.
- 195 critical minerals projects announced since the start of 2026, representing **€64 billion ($74 billion)** in investment.
- The **U.S. launched Project Vault**, a $12 billion critical minerals reserve.
- The **EU shortlisted tungsten, rare earths, and gallium** for its first joint stockpile.

> **Key quote:** *"The 60% target will be challenging... especially in terms of processed rare earths and magnets where China controls 90% of global output."* — Neha Mukherjee, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

---

### 2. China's Rare Earths Curbs Extend Pressure on Supply to Japan
**Date:** June 22, 2026 | **Source:** Reuters / The Financial Express

- **China's exports of heavy rare earths** (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium) to Japan were **negligible in May**, continuing a squeeze since November 2025.
- Export controls were introduced in **April 2025** and tightened in **January–February 2026** after a diplomatic dispute over Taiwan.
- **Rare earth magnet maker Shin-Etsu Chemical** announced plans to build its **first new rare earth refining facility since 2008**.
- **China's rare earth magnet exports** fell **35% month-on-month** in May to their lowest level in a year.

---

**Background context across multiple articles:**

- In **October 2025**, China imposed some of its strictest curbs on **rare earth and permanent magnet exports**, disrupting global supply chains and exposing over-reliance on a single source.
- This is considered one of China's **most effective diplomatic levers**, particularly for heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) critical to high-strength magnets used in EVs, wind turbines, defense systems, and robotics.

---

Here is a summary of the search results for the **DOE Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator** funding opportunity:

## Overview

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) issued a **Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)** (Solicitation # DE-FOA-0003589) for up to **$69 million** through the **Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator Program**, announced on **April 7, 2026**. It is led by the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), the Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office (AMMTO), and the Office of Geothermal (OG).

## Key Deadlines

| Milestone | Date |
|---|---|
| **Letter of Intent (LOI) Deadline** | **April 24, 2026** (required, non-binding) |
| **Topic Area 1 Deadline** | **May 29, 2026** |
| **Topic Area 2 Deadline** | **June 25, 2026** |
| **Topic Area 3 Deadline** | **July 23, 2026** |

## Topic Area 2 (Deadline: June 25, 2026)

The **June 25, 2026 deadline** applies to **Topic Area 2**:

**Processes to refine and alloy gallium, gallium nitride, germanium, and silicon carbide for use in semiconductor applications**

- **Total Funding:** $6 million
- **Expected Awards:** ~1–5
- **Individual Award:** Up to $2 million (Phase 1)
- **Cost Share:** 20%
- **Key focus areas include:**
  - Prototyping processes for purification, refining, solidification, crystallization, powder/ingot formation, and single crystal growth for Ga, GaN, Ge, or SiC to semiconductor-grade purity
  - Reducing reliance on foreign-sourced precursor and process chemicals
  - Producing bulk GaN single crystals or high-purity Ga from domestic sources
  - Reducing critical impurities during processing
  - Alloying processes for semiconductor compounds with controlled stoichiometry

## All Three Topic Areas

| Topic | Deadline | Funding | Focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Topic Area 1** | May 29, 2026 | $24M | Production & material efficiency for critical materials, including REEs from scrap and mine tailings (subtopics 1A, 1B, 1C) |
| **Topic Area 2** | **June 25, 2026** | $6M | Refining & alloying Ga, GaN, Ge, SiC for semiconductors |
| **Topic Area 3** | July 23, 2026 | $23M | Direct lithium extraction, pre/post-treatment, and geothermal exploration (subtopics 3A, 3B, 3C) |

## Structure

The program has two phases:
- **Phase 1** (prototype-scale, TRL 3→6): awards up to $2–$3 million, 20% cost share, up to 36 months
- **Phase 2** (pilot-scale, TRL 6→7): up to $8 million per award, 50% cost share, through December 2029 (open only to Phase 1 awardees)

Eligible applicants include domestic institutions of higher education, for-profit and nonprofit entities, state/local governments, and Indian Tribes. All work must be performed in the United States.

Here are the detailed findings from the web search on the **G7 Critical Minerals Alliance at the Évian 2026 Summit**, with a focus on **permanent magnets and rare earth targets**:

---

## Summit Overview

The 2026 G7 Summit was held in **Évian-les-Bains, France** (June 17–19, 2026), chaired by France. Critical minerals supply chain security was a central priority. Rather than a single joint communiqué, the summit issued **nine thematic declarations** — one of which was a dedicated **Joint Declaration on Securing Supply Chains for Critical Minerals**.

---

## Key Permanent Magnets & Rare Earth Target

**Target: Reduce dependence on any single supplier outside the G7 and partner countries for rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030, with an ambition to reach 50% as soon as possible.**

This was explicitly aimed at reducing reliance on **China**, which currently controls approximately:
- ~70% of global rare earth **production**
- ~90% of global rare earth **processing** capacity
- A dominant share of **permanent magnet** manufacturing

The trigger for this urgency was **China's 2025 export controls on rare earth permanent magnets**, which disrupted Western manufacturing supply chains across EVs, wind turbines, defense (e.g., F-35), and consumer electronics.

---

## G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance

A new **non-binding alliance** was formally established, building on the 2025 Kananaskis G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance. It serves as a platform for:

- **Coordination** on diversification, financing, transparency, stockpiling, and crisis response
- **IEA-led monitoring** — the International Energy Agency provides market analysis and early warnings of supply disruptions
- **Open to like-minded partner countries** (e.g., India, Brazil, South Korea, Kenya attended Évian)

---

## Supporting Mechanisms Announced

| Mechanism | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| **Stockpiling coordination** | G7 members agreed to expand domestic stockpiles and align mechanisms. Japan offered to help other G7 nations build reserves (Japan already has a national critical minerals stockpile) |
| **Traceability & transparency** | Pilot mechanisms launched for **lithium and nickel**, expanding to 5 additional minerals per year (with focus on rare earths) |
| **Recycling** | Joint target to boost recycling capacity to a "significant share" of annual consumption by 2030 |
| **Investment** | 195 critical minerals projects announced since start of 2026, totaling **€64 billion (~$74 billion)** in investment |
| **Potential market tools** | Exploring price-gap subsidies, joint procurement, quotas, and price floors — though the U.S. push for legally binding price interventions faced skepticism from European allies |

---

## Broader Policy Context

- The declaration cited "**grave concerns**" about **non-market policies and economic coercion** (implicitly referencing China)
- The U.S. launched its **$12 billion Project Vault** (critical minerals reserve) earlier in 2026
- The EU had shortlisted tungsten, rare earths, and gallium for its first joint stockpile
- A **2027 DFARS deadline** requires U.S. defense contractors to source rare earth magnets domestically (e.g., the Pentagon committed $500M to Phoenix Tailings' "Freedom Facility" for midstream rare earth processing)
- **Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi** called for coordinated action and highlighted Japan's existing national stockpile system

---

## Challenges Acknowledged

Analysts (including **Benchmark Mineral Intelligence**'s Neha Mukherjee) noted:
- The 60% target is **ambitious** given China's 90%+ grip on rare earth processing
- Japan has tried to reduce its rare earth reliance since **2010** but still sources ~75-80% from China
- Building alternative **midstream processing** capacity (not just mining) is the harder bottleneck
- The alliance is **non-binding** — implementation depends on whether policy support translates into actual investment

---

## Sources

- [Bloomberg: G7 aims to see China supply no more than 60% of rare earths](https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/g7-aims-to-ensure-china-supplies-no-more-than-60-of-rare-earths)

6. Policy, Regulation and Strategic Context

G7 Summit — Critical Minerals Alliance Launched (Évian, 17–19 June 2026)

G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance: At the 2026 G7 Summit in Évian-les-Bains, leaders announced a dedicated Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance to reduce dependence on any single supplier of rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030 (with an ambition of 50%). The IEA will provide market monitoring and early warning of supply disruptions. Traceability and transparency pilot mechanisms will start with lithium and nickel, expanding to five new critical minerals each year. The G7 also agreed to explore joint procurement, price-gap subsidies, quotas, and price floors to support non-Chinese supply chains. 195 critical minerals projects have been announced since the start of 2026, representing €64 billion ($74 billion) in investment.

European Union — Three-Supplier Rule Drafted

EU Drafts "Three-Supplier Rule" for Critical Supply Chains (June 2026): The European Commission is drafting a mandatory "three-supplier rule" that would require companies in sensitive sectors to source critical components and raw materials from at least three different suppliers in different countries, with a single-supplier cap of ~30–40%. The rule covers critical raw materials, chemicals, EV batteries, rare earths, and pharmaceuticals. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič publicly announced the proposal on 5 June 2026. The rule would apply to large companies initially, with transition periods for SMEs. Discussions are expected at the EU leaders' summit. The rule faces WTO compatibility concerns from China and cost-burden criticism from industry.

The rule covers critical raw materials, chemicals, EV batteries, rare earths, and pharmaceuticals. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič publicly announced the proposal on 5 June 2026. The rule would apply to large companies initially, with transition periods for SMEs. Discussions are expected at the EU leaders' summit.
